players.product: Server PCBs (high-layer-count, high-speed boards for general-purpose and AI servers supporting Intel, AMD and Arm CPUs; PCIe 6.0 server PCBs in small-volume ramp), plus accelerator-card, optical-module and switch PCBs

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record, Q3 results pre-announcement briefing; deputy GM and board secretary Zeng Yangqing): per the pre-announcement, Jan-Sep 2026 net profit attributable is expected at RMB 14.5-15 hundred million, up about 100.33%-107.23%, and net profit excluding non-recurring items RMB 14.2-14.7 hundred million, up about 101.84%-108.94%, on compute-hardware demand for general-purpose server, AI server, switch and accelerator-card PCBs. The Thailand plant completed core-customer audits on plan, became a second engine of compute-product sales growth and was profitable in the period; Huangshi Delton's profitability improved year over year.
quarterly_data.figure: Jan-Sep 2026 net profit attributable expected RMB 14.5-15 hundred million (+100.33%-107.23%)

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): recently some compute customers were short of CPUs and memory chips, so their materials were incomplete and production was not started on time, which affected the company's PCB shipments and its Q3 results to some extent; management says this is a temporary customer material shortage, not a change in demand, and its full-year expectations are unchanged. Its own production did not stop and lines ran at full load through the National Day holiday; it is prioritizing orders that can be picked up immediately so as not to add inventory. It expects CCL-led raw-material supply to stay tight and the imbalance hard to resolve fully before H2 2027; its CCL is mainly high-speed material, so the cost impact is controllable.

Management (IR record): PCIe 6.0 product prices are expected to rise versus the previous generation with higher layer counts and material grades; some platforms have started small-batch shipments and other platforms are expected to ship in Q1 or Q2 2027, depending on chip mass-production timing. The Thailand base currently makes mainly general-purpose compute boards because the local supply chain is thin and many materials come from mainland China; more AI orders will follow as its capability and local supply improve. Equipment added to Thailand phase 1 with H-share proceeds is being installed and commissioned, with production starting progressively in Q4 2026 and new capacity in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: PCIe 6.0: some platforms in small-batch shipment, others Q1/Q2 2027; Thailand added capacity from Q4 2026
